text:
Both of these teams played last night, and only one of them is enjoying the morning after. The Blues came from behind in the third to beat Dallas 5-3 and have points in six straight. The Capitals lost 3-2 at home to Florida when Sam Bennett scored with 24 seconds left, his 200th career goal, and they are 1-4-0 in their last five. A week of Ovechkin celebrations, including the ceremony for his franchise assist record, has been the warm part of a cold stretch in Washington.

The quiet subplot in St. Louis is the crease. ESPN reported this week that Joel Hofer has taken over as the starter from Jordan Binnington, and our projection has Binnington back in for the second half of the back-to-back. His numbers explain the change: an .845 save percentage and 7.5 goals allowed above what his shots deserved, after a season last year that was 22.9 goals below expected. Charlie Lindgren, likely in goal for Washington, is not far off at minus 6.5. Neither crease is a fortress.

Here is the odd part of the Blues' run: they have won it without owning the puck. Over the last five they got 45% of the expected goals, the measure of chance quality, and they have done it without Jimmy Snuggerud, their 20-point winger, who is on injured reserve. Dylan Holloway has stepped into his spot beside Robert Thomas and Jake Neighbours and is up to 20 minutes a night. Thomas has 17 points in his last 10. Washington has been the better five-on-five team this season at 54% of the expected goals, but it takes over four penalties a game.

Watch Ryan Leonard, the 2023 eighth overall pick, who carries a seven-game point streak into a game against a goalie who has struggled. And Connor McMichael faces the Capitals for the first time since leaving them after 315 games, with Jordan Kyrou, the player on the other side of that ledger, out injured for Washington.
headline: Two tired teams, one goalie job up for grabs
